name: Distinct subset sums extremal problem and inverse theorems for few subset sums
description: Erdos asked whether an n-element set of positive integers with all 2^n subset sums distinct must have largest element at least c 2^n. Best known: f(n) >= (sqrt(2/pi)-o(1)) 2^n/sqrt(n) (Elkies-Gleason, Dubroff-Fox-Xu) with finite form f(n) >= C(n,floor(n/2)); Costa-Della Fiore (arXiv 2609.27941) improve the finite bound to the hypercube bandwidth f(n) >= sum_{j<n} C(j,floor(j/2)). Upper bound: Bohman 0.22002 * 2^n. At the other extreme, inverse theorems classify sets with FEW subset sums: Carpenter-Defant-Kravitz (2605.05498) and Chen (2609.00044) show that with at most C(n+1,2)+1+M sums the set is a dilation of an integer set of small total sum (near homogeneous AP), with Chen handling M = n + C exactly via integer partitions. Korsky (2606.24139) treats subset-sum sets free of k-term APs (bandwidth of the ternary grid for k=3). Hegyvari-Pham-Xue (2609.14630) is about density realization in locally finite abelian groups, not an AP-free construction.
authors_year_venue: Costa and Della Fiore, arXiv:2609.27941 (stamped 22 Aug 2026), math.CO; Dubroff, Fox, Xu, SIAM J. Discrete Math 35 (2021) 322-324; Carpenter, Defant, Kravitz, 'Sets with few subset sums', arXiv:2605.05498v2 (24 Aug 2026); Chen, 'Fixed-defect inverse theorems for subset sums', arXiv:2609.00044v3 (14 Sep 2026); Korsky, 'Arithmetic progression-free subset-sum sets', arXiv:2606.24139 (22 Jun 2026); Hegyvari, Pham, Xue, 'Subset-sum density realization in locally finite abelian groups', arXiv:2609.14630v1 (13 Sep 2026); Bohman, EJC 5 (1998) R3; Steinerberger, IJNT 19 (2023).
status_and_verification: All preprints (arXiv), none checked for refereed publication. Read in full via alphaXiv text: 2609.27941 (all sections), 2609.00044 (all sections incl. proofs), 2606.24139 (all sections). 2605.05498: abstract, introduction and statements of Theorems 1.1-1.3 only; proofs not read, and the end of the statement of Thm 1.2 was truncated in extraction. 2609.14630: abstract and introduction only. Dubroff-Fox-Xu itself not read; its bound is as quoted by Costa-Della Fiore. Note: the item description attributes 2609.14630 to 'AP-free and density-realization'; the AP-free paper is 2606.24139, 2609.14630 is the density-realization paper.
key_theorem_or_bound: [uncertain] (a) Costa-Della Fiore Thm 1.1: for all n, f(n) >= H_n := sum_{j=0}^{n-1} C(j,floor(j/2)) = bw(Q_n) (Harper); H_n > C(n,floor(n/2)) for n >= 3; H_n/C(n,floor(n/2)) = 1+2/(3n)+O(n^-2) (n even), 1+4/(3n)+O(n^-2) (n odd); so f(n) >= sqrt(2/pi) 2^n/sqrt(n) (1+5/(12n)) even, (1+7/(12n)) odd. Key step: ordering all 2^n subsets by subset sum gives a numbering of the hypercube of bandwidth <= a_n. (b) CDK Thm 1.1: n>=4, 0<=M<=n-4: |FS(A)| <= C(n+1,2)+1+M iff A is inside a*Z_{>0} and sum(a^{-1}A) <= C(n+1,2)+M. CDK Thm 1.2: |FS(A)| <= C n^2 gives A = A1 u A2 with A1 inside r*Z, sum(r^{-1}A1) <<_C n^2 and A2 small (exact bound on |A2| truncated in extraction). CDK Thm 1.3: in R^d, if every proper subspace holds <= (1-eps)n points then |FS(A)| >= gamma_d(eps) n^{d+1}. (c) Chen Thm 1.1: for fixed C >= -1 and n >= N_C (N_{-1}=68, N_0=69), |FS(A)| <= C(n+1,2)+n+C+1 iff A=lambda*B with sum(B) <= C(n+1,2)+n+C, or A = lambda*E_n(m,pi) with m in {1,2}, pi a partition of C+m or C+m+1; number of exceptional classes P(C+1)+2P(C+2)+P(C+3). (d) Korsky: g_3(n) >= (T_n-1)/2 + sum_{j<n} T_j ~ (sqrt3/(2 sqrt(pi))) 3^n/sqrt(n) (T_n central trinomial); g_k(n) >>_k ((k-1)/(k-2))^n n^{-log2((k-1)/(k-2))} for k>=4; limsup g_k^{1/n} <= min_{p prime>=3} p^{2/(min(p,k)-1)}. (e) HPX: for a countable locally finite abelian group G, |2G|=infinity iff every [alpha,beta] in [0,1] is the set of limit points of |P(A) cap G_i|/|G_i| for some A.
regime_exponents: [uncertain] Magnitude regime: distinct sums need max a >= about 2^n/sqrt(n) (exponent 1 in n, times 1/sqrt n); Bohman gives 0.22 * 2^n so dissociated sets live at magnitude exponent about n bits. Inverse theorems cover only |FS(A)| <= O(n^2) (quadratic regime), i.e. exponent 0 in n; nothing at 2^{0.311n}, 2^{0.5n} or 2^{0.661n} for the number of subset sums. The n/2 baseline is not touched. A set with 2^{0.311n}-ish half sums is in the unexplored gap between poly(n) and 2^n.
proof_type_and_tools: Combinatorial/graph-theoretic (hypercube bandwidth, Harper; ternary grid bandwidth, Billera-Blanco) for the extremal lower bounds; additive-combinatorial (Kneser's theorem, DeVos-Goddyn-Mohar-Samal quadratic lower bound |FS(R)| >= |H|+|R\H|^2/64, Lev's consecutive subset sums, stabiliser arguments in R/xZ) for the inverse theorems; carry-free digit constructions on graphs for upper bounds (Korsky).
quantitative_loss: Extremal bounds lose only a polynomial factor (sqrt n) against 2^n; the 2609.27941 improvement is a 1+O(1/n) factor, with an explicit remark in Korsky that bandwidth barriers (Remark 4.5) cannot be beaten without extra arithmetic rigidity. Inverse theorems have effective but huge thresholds (N_C = 68 already for C=-1) and are polynomial-regime only; they do not survive exponential energy.
worst_case_vs_average_case: All results are worst case over sets (adversarial). No random-input statement. Extremal constructions (Bohman, powers of 3/digit sets) are explicit worst-case hard families.
coefficient_set: {0,1} subset sums (sets, distinct elements) for the distinct-sums and few-sums results; Korsky's k=3 case is equivalent to injectivity on {0,1,2}^n (bounded-coefficient dissociation); CDK Thm 1.2/1.3 allow real positive sets and R^d vectors; Chen works with positive real sets.
subset_size_regime: All subsets (2^n sums), no size restriction. Costa-Della Fiore's bandwidth argument uses all vertices of the hypercube; a layer-restricted (Theta(n)-size) variant is not given.
relevance_to_Nc: Distinct-subset-sums sets are exactly N_c = 0 for ALL sizes, so they set the minimum magnitude (about 2^n/sqrt n) at which zero relations is possible: if all |a_i| < C(n,n/2) then some equal-sum disjoint pair exists. For C1 this gives existence only; the guaranteed pair may be short, not Theta(n). Inverse theorems say the other extreme (few sums, many collisions) is a near-homogeneous AP.
relevance_to_Dstar: Few distinct subset sums forces rank-1 structure (commensurable, near-AP), which makes D* tiny but the instance easy (small total sum, pseudo-polynomial DP). That matches the repo observation that low D* appears only on arithmetic progressions. Sets with D* <= 2^{0.311n} but exponential magnitude are not classified by any of these theorems; Bohman/Sidon-like dissociated sets sit at the opposite end (maximal D*).
applicability_gap: Inverse theorems stop at |FS(A)| = O(n^2) while D* <= 2^{0.311n} is exponentially larger; extremal bounds concern total distinctness not Theta(n)-subsets or half-sums; real versus integer, {0,1} fine; polynomial-doubling hypotheses are not present; bandwidth/isoperimetric methods give existence of ONE collision, not a count of N_c.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: Bohman sets (0.22002 * 2^n), Conway-Guy sequences, powers of 3 and base-p restricted-digit sets (Korsky: A_r = {p^i} u {p^i+p^j : edge ij}, max < 2 p^{r-1}); near-extremal pairs where |FS| = C(n+1,2)+n+C+1 (the Chen exceptional family: initial interval minus {1} or {2} plus a partition tail); rank-d GAPs with random generators.
dependency_chain: [uncertain] Feeds inverse_littlewood_offord (few sums vs concentrated sums), dissociated_sidon_structure (dense side), fourier_large_spectrum_bohr (Steinerberger's Fourier proof of the 2^n/sqrt n bound is the L^2/L^4 view of the same objects). Could be composed with a counting argument to turn 'sums < 2^n/sqrt n implies a relation' into a quantitative N_c lower bound via second moments (Erdos-Moser).
constructiveness: The bounds are existence statements; Chen's classification gives an explicit finite-state description of the exceptional sets for fixed C (Thm 7.3, automaton); Korsky's upper constructions are explicit (graph + carry-free digits). No search algorithm for relations.
lean_formalizable: [uncertain] The elementary parts (|FS(A)| >= C(n+1,2)+1, the bandwidth <= a_n proposition, Catalan identities H_{2r}=C(2r,r)+Gamma_r) look formalizable without mathlib; Harper's bandwidth theorem and Kneser would be the expensive imports.
computational_check: [uncertain] Sources: Korsky enumerated g_3(n) for n<=4 (g_3(4)=22 > 21=b_4); Costa-Della Fiore and Chen are proof-only (Chen's thresholds N_C are about 68-69 so the theorem is not testable at n<=40). In the repo, brute force f(n) for n<=8 and collision counts of Bohman/Conway-Guy sets at n<=40 are feasible with scripts/analysis.
next_experiment: Compute N_c (equal-sum disjoint pairs with both sizes between 0.1n and 0.4n) for random integer sets with magnitudes 2^{cn}, c from 0.3 to 1.2 at n=24,28,32, and mark the threshold where N_c drops to 0; compare with the 2^n/sqrt(n) distinct-sums threshold to see whether the Theta(n)-size relations disappear at the same c.
open_issues: Erdos's 2^n conjecture (f(n) >= c 2^n) is still open; the bandwidth method is exhausted by the barrier remark in Korsky; the 2609.27941 arXiv id month (09) disagrees with its stamped date (22 Aug 2026), which is a minor metadata oddity; CDK Thm 1.2 truncated in extraction; none of the inverse theorems reach super-polynomial |FS|.
